Mr. Speaker, I regret to have to inform this house that the first I learned of the results of two studies that were commissioned by the government on May 1, was last night after one of the firms had held a press conference.
In answer to the hon. member's question I may say that in May through the Department of Industry the government had commissioned two studies respecting the design, development and supply of a domestic satellite communications system. The contracts were let at a cost of approximately $550,000. The part that bothers me is that neither I nor my colleague the Minister of Industry, Trade and Commerce has yet received such reports.
I see that one of the companies, and the other company this morning, are prepared to launch satellites of a certain size and design. speechtext: Mr. Speaker, my question is for the Minister of National Health and Welfare. speechtext: On the orders of the day:

subtopic: COMPLAINTS FROM FARM PUBLICATIONS AS TO INCREASED RATES
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, my question is for the Postmaster General. Has the minister received representations from farm magazine publishers to the effect that many of them may have to cease publication after the new postal rates come into effect? If so, has the minister considered the situation.

subtopic: COMPLAINTS FROM FARM PUBLICATIONS AS TO INCREASED RATES
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I received a number of such representations prior to the adoption of the bill. I pointed out to those making representations that in most cases they could cover the increased cost simply by increasing their subscription rates by as little as 35 cents a year.
